title: Mechanical builds
oneLiner: BlockParty, a fully autonomous robot my team built that won the Best Design Award in ME 2110, Georgia Tech’s sophomore design course. Plus high school FIRST Robotics Competition (FRC): the pneumatics on two robots, and second in command on the swerve drivetrain.
cardSummary: Autonomous robot that won ME 2110’s Best Design Award, plus high school robot pneumatics
metaDescription: I helped build BlockParty, the autonomous robot that won ME 2110’s Best Design Award at Georgia Tech, and owned the pneumatics on two FIRST robots.
whatIOwnedSummary: BlockParty: a team project, so these were team decisions. My part: prototyping and fabricating our first mechanism (the sprint 1 ore intake), laser-cutting parts for another, ideation and testing on the bag arm, and the code for our first sprint. FRC: I owned the pneumatics on both robots, and was second in command on the swerve drivetrain: some of the CAD, building some of the swerve modules and the one-piece bumpers, fabrication, and training rookies to build the rest.

claims.title: BlockParty (ME 2110 Creative Decisions & Design, Jan–May 2025): a fully autonomous robot that won the course’s Best Design Award
claims.requirementOrConstraint: Three judged sprints building toward a fully autonomous robot.
claims.method: We generated concepts with a morph chart and chose among them with a weighted evaluation matrix. Over the three sprints, we designed, fabricated, and tested the mechanisms: pneumatic pistons, solenoids, motors, and mouse-trap actuators, under Arduino control.
claims.resultMetric: The robot ran fully autonomously in competition.

claims.title: BlockParty sprint 1 (Feb 2025): prototyped and built the ore intake, a static ramp first, then a motor
claims.requirementOrConstraint: Sprint 1: get to the rotating tower and sweep its ore onto our side of the field.
claims.method: Our first version had no moving parts: a static ramp shaped like a /, so the rotating tower would carry the ore onto it and down into our field. Testing showed the ore could ride the tower without ever sliding off, so we added a motor that sweeps it off instead of waiting for it to fall. The clips show the motor version being tested on the tower's top in February, and the sprint 1 carriage parked against the rotating tower.
claims.resultMetric: The ramp alone didn't always work: sometimes the ore just slipped along the tower as it rotated and never slid off. We switched to a motor that sweeps the ore off. I prototyped and fabricated the mechanism.

claims.title: FRC pneumatics, Excelsior and Jim (High school, 2022–2023): Director of Pneumatics
claims.method: Installed the compressors, set pressure and flow regulators so each mechanism got the right force and piston extension speed, added manual and automatic release valves for safety, and routed the tubing so every mechanism got the supply it needed.
claims.resultMetric: Owned the pneumatic systems on two robots end to end, and kept them working through each season: patching leaks at the tank, and recutting tubing that had been cut at an angle so the fittings sealed.

claims.title: FRC drivetrain, Excelsior and Jim (High school, 2022–2023): second in command on the swerve drivetrain
claims.method: Did some of the drivetrain CAD, built and tested some of the swerve modules, built the one-piece bumpers, and fabricated parts.
claims.resultMetric: Trained rookies to build the rest of the swerve modules. At competitions I kept the modules running, repairing any that were damaged in a match.

outcome: BlockParty won the Best Design Award in ME 2110 and ran fully autonomously. On FRC, I owned the pneumatics on both robots and trained rookies to build the rest of the swerve modules.
